The words

If listening, as I listen still,
O God! to thine instructive word,
In spite of all my spirit's will,
Some whispering voice of doubt is heard, —
That voice spontaneous from the soul,
Which nought can check and nought control;

If when most earnestly I pray
For light, for aid, for strength from thee,
Some struggling thoughts will force their way,
And break my soul's serenity; —
If reason, thy best gift, will hold
The sceptre only half controlled: —

Help and forgive! heaven's alphabet
Hath many a word of mystery;
I read not all thy record yet,
Though perseveringly I try;
But teach me, Lord! and none shall be
More prompt, more pleased to learn of thee.

How to sing it from the solfa

  • Find doh first. Play or hum Ab and sing d r m f s up from it, so the whole choir has the key in their ears before you start.
  • Pitch the first note. The tune starts on s (E♭), on the word “If”, as a pickup before the first full bar.
  • Count the time. 3/2 means three minim beats in each bar. In the grid every cell is half a crotchet: a dash (–) holds the note before it, and _ is a rest.
  • Know the notes. The tune uses d r m f s l t and the chromatic fe. A comma after a note (s,) is the octave below; an apostrophe (d') is the octave above.

About the hymn

John Bowring wrote these words. They were printed in Hymns for Christian Devotion, compiled by John G. Adams and Edwin H. Chapin (Boston, 1846), as hymn 465 of its twenty-second edition (1853), “"Help thou my unbelief."”.

The book printed the words without tunes, marked Long Metre, six lines (8.8.8.8.8.8), to be sung to any tune of that metre. This page sets them to SELENA; any other Long Metre, six lines tune fits them as well.

  • Words: John Bowring (1792–1872)
  • Music (1850): Isaac B. Woodbury (1819–1858)

Questions about If Listening, as I Listen Still

What is the doh of If Listening, as I Listen Still?

In this version, in Ab major, doh is Ab. If your choir sings it in another key, doh moves to the new key note and every solfa syllable stays the same — that is what movable doh means.

What note does If Listening, as I Listen Still start on?

It starts on s (E♭ in Ab major), a pickup on the word “If” before the first full bar. Find doh first, then sing up or down to s.

Is If Listening, as I Listen Still in the public domain?

Yes. John Bowring died in 1872, Isaac B. Woodbury died in 1858; the words were in print by 1853 and the music in 1850. Everyone named died before 1955 and both were published before 1929, so the hymn is out of copyright in the UK, the EU, the United States and Nigeria. Modern arrangements and translations can still be under copyright.
